questions.text: Give ONE advantage and ONE limitation of using public-key (asymmetric) encryption for secure messages.

questions.aiReferenceNotes: Asymmetric encryption uses two related keys: a public key that may be shared and a private key that must be protected. Explain the pair of keys. State a genuine strength. State a genuine practical limit. Do not claim public keys must remain secret.

1. Explain the pair of keys.
2. State a genuine strength.
3. State a genuine practical limit.

Example: A web service negotiates a symmetric session key using public-key methods and then uses fast symmetric encryption for bulk traffic.

questions.text: Why do replicated databases need synchronization after records are changed?
questions.correctAnswer: Synchronization propagates or reconciles changes among replicas so that readers do not continue using conflicting or stale copies and agreed consistency rules are respected.
questions.aiReferenceNotes: A database replica is another copy of data, often placed on another server. Describe that changes happen on one or more copies. Explain how synchronization keeps the copies acceptably consistent. Replication does not automatically replace backups or resolve every conflict.
questions.explanation:
A database replica is another copy of data, often placed on another server.

How to build your answer:
1. Describe that changes happen on one or more copies.
2. Explain how synchronization keeps the copies acceptably consistent.

Example: A new booking must appear at a second branch after replication.

Student note: Replication does not automatically replace backups or resolve every conflict.

questions.text: SecondShelf is a community web service for trading used study materials. A registered seller adds an item with a title, condition and price. Buyers search available listings and buy an item. The service records a purchase and its chosen listing, marks the item as sold, and sends notifications. The seller confirms dispatch, and the buyer may report a delivery problem. The service keeps seller ratings after a completed purchase. Draw a UML domain class diagram with key concepts, attributes, links and sensible multiplicities.
questions.correctAnswer: Customer(customerId,name,email) has Listings as Seller; Listing(listingId,title,condition,price,status) belongs to Seller and may be purchased in one Purchase; Purchase(purchaseId,date,status) links Buyer and Listing; Shipment(shipmentId,date,status) belongs to Purchase; Rating(score,comment) optionally relates Buyer, Purchase and Seller. Multiplicities reflect 1 seller to many listings, 1 buyer to many purchases, and 1 purchase to 1 listing.

questions.text: SecondShelf is a community web service for trading used study materials. A registered seller adds an item with a title, condition and price. Buyers search available listings and buy an item. The service records a purchase and its chosen listing, marks the item as sold, and sends notifications. The seller confirms dispatch, and the buyer may report a delivery problem. The service keeps seller ratings after a completed purchase. Write a FULLY DEVELOPED use case description for the goal 'Buy listed item'. Include a name, primary actor, trigger, preconditions, normal steps, at least two alternative/exception flows and a clear success condition.
questions.correctAnswer: Use case Buy listed item. Primary actor Buyer. Trigger: buyer chooses Buy on an available listing. Preconditions: buyer has an active authenticated account; listing available. Main flow: buyer selects item, system shows price/detail, buyer confirms delivery/payment, system validates details, authorizes payment, records Purchase, marks Listing sold, notifies seller and buyer. Alternatives: payment declined -> show reason and allow retry; listing already sold -> stop transaction and inform buyer; missing address -> request correction. Postconditions: purchase recorded and item unavailable, or no sale if failed.
aiRubric: Sequential normal flow with actor/system responsibilities
questions.aiReferenceNotes: A fully developed use case describes one actor goal in enough detail to understand normal and exceptional interactions. Name the goal and actor, then state the trigger and preconditions. Write the numbered happy path, alternating actor actions and system responses. Add alternatives/exceptions and postconditions. Use a numbered user/system flow; a loose paragraph of features is not a fully developed use case.
questions.explanation:
A fully developed use case describes one actor goal in enough detail to understand normal and exceptional interactions.

How to build your answer:
1. Name the goal and actor, then state the trigger and preconditions.
2. Write the numbered happy path, alternating actor actions and system responses.
3. Add alternatives/exceptions and postconditions.

Example: If another buyer purchases first, the system should block this checkout rather than sell an unavailable listing.

Student note: Use a numbered user/system flow; a loose paragraph of features is not a fully developed use case.
